headline: The Landscaper Foundation
threshold: By Lesson 10, you can greet clients and crew, give numbers, times and measurements, describe the yard and tools, ask simple questions, make polite requests and ask for help, and start Landscaper Lesson 1.

lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say the Spanish sounds in common yard and tool words and greet clients and crew politely.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr, silent h and the written accent; greetings

words.note: Spanish a is always 'ah': PAH-lah.
rr is a rolled r; ll sounds like English y: ca-rre-TEE-ya.
Roll the rr: TYEH-rra.
j sounds like a strong English h; the accent marks the stress: har-DEEN.
The h is silent and the j is a strong English h: O-hahs.
ch sounds like the ch in church.
The accent puts the stress on the first syllable: AR-bol.
The outdoor faucet; ll sounds like y: YAH-veh.
In gue the u is silent and the g is hard: man-GEH-ra.
Use until noon; after that say buenas tardes.

words.en: My name is Ana, nice to meet you.

words.note: Formal, for clients. With coworkers say ¿Cómo estás?

lessons.speaking: Greet a homeowner and a crew member, say your name, and name three tools or yard words with clear vowels, rr and j.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Give start times and simple yard measurements and quantities in feet, pounds, gallons and bags.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and feet, square feet, pounds and bags with de

words.note: As a measurement; plural los pies (10 pies).

words.en: We start at 7 in the morning.
words.es: Empezamos a las 7 de la mañana.
words.note: Use a las + number for 'at' a time.

words.en: We finish at 4:30 in the afternoon.
words.es: Terminamos a las 4:30 de la tarde.
words.note: Say 4:30 as las cuatro y media.

words.en: The yard measures 40 feet by 25 feet.
words.es: El patio mide 40 pies por 25 pies.
El jardín es de 1,000 pies cuadrados.
words.note: Measurements take de: es de 1,000 pies cuadrados.

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member what time you start and finish today, how big the yard is in feet, and how many bags of soil you need.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Describe grass, soil and tools and say where equipment is with ser and estar.
lessons.focus: ser for what something is, estar for its condition or location

words.note: Common in Mexico for brown; it does not change for gender.
A woman is la encargada.
estar: a condition that can change.

words.en: The mower is in the truck.
words.es: La podadora está en la troca.
words.note: estar for location.

words.es: El tanque de gasolina está vacío.

words.note: ser: what something is.
ser for who you are; a woman says la encargada.

lessons.speaking: Describe a yard to a crew member: say if the grass is tall or short and the soil dry or wet, where the mower is, and who the crew lead is.

lessons.title: Have, There Is, Need and Want
lessons.objective: Say what tools and supplies you have, need or want, and what must be done first.
lessons.focus: tener, hay, necesitar, querer and hay que + infinitive

words.note: Feminine noun that takes el: el agua fría.
Common US Spanish loanword on job sites.
Common US Spanish loanword.

words.en: I have the gloves in the truck.
words.es: Tengo los guantes en la troca.

words.en: Is there gas for the mower?
words.note: hay means there is / there are.
usted form, polite to a coworker or client.

words.en: You have to turn off the mower before cleaning it.
words.es: Hay que apagar la podadora antes de limpiarla.
words.note: hay que + infinitive: something everyone must do.

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member what tools you have in the truck, what you need, and one thing you have to do before using the mower.

lessons.title: Go, Do and Can
lessons.objective: Say where you are going on a job site, what you plan to do, and ask if you can use a tool.
lessons.focus: ir, ir a + infinitive for plans, hacer, poder

words.note: Mexican usage.
a + el becomes al.

words.en: We're going to cut the front yard grass.
words.es: Vamos a cortar el pasto del patio de enfrente.
words.note: ir a + infinitive for plans.

words.en: Can I use the leaf blower?
After lunch we're going to the nursery.
words.es: Después del almuerzo vamos al vivero.

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member where you are going next, what you are going to do there, and ask if you can use the blower.

lessons.title: Present Tense
lessons.objective: Say who does each yard task and when, using present tense verbs.
lessons.focus: Regular -ar, -er, -ir present endings for yo, tú, usted, nosotros, ellos

words.note: Common in Mexico; you may also hear el zacate.

words.en: I cut the grass and you sweep the sidewalk.
words.es: Yo corto el pasto y tú barres la banqueta.
words.note: tú is informal, between coworkers.

words.en: I plant the flowers in the shade.
words.es: Yo planto las flores en la sombra.
words.note: -ar verb: yo planto, tú plantas, nosotros plantamos.
-ir verb: vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, viven.

words.es: Nosotros trabajamos de lunes a viernes.

words.en: They pick up the branches and the leaves.
words.es: Ellos recogen las ramas y las hojas.
words.note: -er verb: ellos ending is -en.

lessons.speaking: Tell a coworker who does each task today: you cut, they sweep, the others pick up branches, and which days your crew works.

lessons.title: Questions
lessons.objective: Ask a homeowner or crew lead simple questions about the job, the place and the time.
lessons.focus: Question words: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cuánto, cómo, por qué, cuál

words.note: Agrees with the noun: ¿cuántas bolsas?, ¿cuántos pies?
Two words with an accent; porque (one word) means because.
Use ¿Cuál es...? for 'what is' a specific thing, like an address.

words.es: ¿Quién es el dueño de la casa?

lessons.speaking: Ask your crew lead the address of the next job, when you start, who the homeowner is, and what you do first.

lessons.title: No, Never and How Much
lessons.objective: Say what is missing, not done yet, or needed more or less of on a yard job.
lessons.focus: Negatives no, nunca, nadie, nada, todavía no; and más, menos, otro

words.note: Spanish uses the double negative: No necesito nada.
Never say un otro: otro rastrillo, otra bolsa.

words.es: No hay nadie en la casa.

words.en: We haven't finished the backyard yet.
words.es: Todavía no terminamos el patio de atrás.

words.en: We need another bag of soil.
We never use the mower without safety glasses.
words.es: Nunca usamos la podadora sin lentes de seguridad.

lessons.speaking: Tell your crew lead what is not done yet, that nobody is home, and that you need another bag of soil and more trash bags.

lessons.title: Polite Requests and Commands
lessons.objective: Make polite requests to a homeowner and give simple usted commands to one worker.
lessons.focus: ¿Puede + infinitive? for requests; usted commands (mueva, traiga, espere)

words.note: Say it when you pass by someone or enter a space.

words.en: Can you open the gate, please?
words.note: ¿Puede + infinitive? is a polite request to one person (usted).

words.en: Can you bring the dog inside, please?
words.note: al perro: use the personal a before a pet as the direct object.

words.en: Please move the car out of the driveway.
words.es: Mueva el carro de la entrada, por favor.
words.note: usted command; to the whole crew say muevan.
usted command; to the whole crew say traigan.

words.en: Can you send me a text tomorrow?

lessons.speaking: Ask a homeowner politely to open the gate, bring the dog inside and move the car, then ask one worker to bring the ladder.

lessons.title: Words You Already Know and Getting Help
lessons.objective: Recognize Spanish words that look like English and ask for help when you don't understand.
lessons.focus: Cognates ending in -ción, -dad, -ente; survival phrases for getting help

words.note: -ción often matches English -tion or -ion.
Also means station.
-dad often matches English -ty.
A woman is la clienta.

words.en: I don't understand, can you repeat?
How do you say 'rake' in Spanish?

words.note: usted command; in the US, 911 is the emergency number.

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member you don't understand, ask them to repeat more slowly, ask how to say a tool in Spanish, and ask for help.
